target.title: fix(gateway): force-discard ACP runtime after cancel/close timeout
target.body:
Closes #106631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who send `/reset` after an ACP-backed session hits a stuck cancel/close (for example after a model/API error poisoned the session) would still get the same broken runtime on the next message. The gateway timed out ACP cancel/close, returned “try again in a moment,” and left the cached runtime handle in place, so recovery required restarting the whole gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

When ACP cancel or close hits the bounded cleanup timeout, the gateway now calls a manager-owned `forceDiscardSession` path that **detaches** the cached runtime handle immediately **outside** the session actor queue (a timed-out cancel may still own that queue) and best-effort closes the detached runtime without awaiting a second hang. Session-reset then continues into the existing fresh-reset / meta path so the next message cannot reuse the stale process. Normal successful cancel→close is unchanged.

Compatibility: additive manager method only; no config, protocol, or public CLI shape changes. Performance: force-discard runs only on the timeout recovery path. Usability: `/reset` can recover without a gateway restart. Security: only the session being reset/deleted is discarded; no auth or approval widening.

## User Impact

Operators and channel users whose ACP session gets stuck can recover with `/reset` even when cancel/close times out, instead of needing a full gateway restart that disrupts every session.

## Evidence

Focused local Vitest on macOS (Crabbox not used):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-handles.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts

# results
✓ manager.runtime-handles.test.ts (14 tests) — force-discard eviction + hanging-close detach
✓ server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts (22 tests) — cancel-timeout and close-timeout force-discard
```

Path-scoped formatting: `oxfmt` on the four touched files — pass.
`git diff --check` — pass.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: `/reset` (and session-delete cleanup) no longer leaves a reusable ACP runtime handle when cancel or close hits the bounded cleanup timeout. Force-discard **detaches the cache entry immediately**, then best-effort closes the detached runtime **without awaiting**, so a second hang on process close cannot stall reset/delete recovery.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout; focused Vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (Verification host: local macOS, Crabbox bypass).
- Current-main contrast: on current main, `closeAcpRuntimeForSession` returns `UNAVAILABLE` on cancel/close timeout without clearing the runtime handle cache, so the next message can reuse the same process.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/control-plane/manager.runtime-handles.test.ts -t "force-discards"`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.reset-cleanup.test.ts -t "force-discards ACP"`
  3. Full sibling suites for both files as listed in Evidence (14 + 22 tests).
- Evidence after fix:
  - Manager (cancel still owns actor): `forceDiscardSession` detaches/closes with `reason: session-reset`; next turn re-ensures (`ensureSession` twice).
  - Manager (hanging runtime close): `forceDiscardSession` **resolves without waiting** on a never-resolving `runtime.close`; next turn still re-ensures a fresh session.
  - Gateway cancel-timeout: short cleanup timeout + hanging cancel → `sessions.reset` succeeds, `forceDiscardSession` once for `agent:main:main` / `session-reset`, no `closeSession`, fresh ACP meta restored.
  - Gateway close-timeout: cancel succeeds, hanging `closeSession` times out → `forceDiscardSession` once; reset still completes and restores pending ACP meta.
- Control check: normal happy-path `sessions.reset closes ACP runtime handles for ACP sessions` still expects `closeSession` and does not force-discard; only the timeout branches use force-discard.
- Observed result after fix: both cancel-timeout and close-timeout reset paths recover without leaving a reusable stale handle, and force-discard cannot re-block on a stuck process close.
- What was not tested: live Telegram/Feishu ACP channel recording with a real stuck backend process; full 15s production cleanup timeout wall-clock (tests use a short override for the race only).
